correctness.rationale: For the repaired RESULT.md. In each lateral face the outward normal is s e_j+e_z/2 with plane offset qρ/2, so the foot is in the apex–edge-midpoint segment (its height lies strictly between 0 and qρ) and the base foot is the centroid. The lateral feet give a positive new base radius and the original base foot is across the origin. Normalizing gives the displayed p,q iteration and its invertible u,v form. The two identities for 2vw−1 and 1+w² give both the invariant H and the positive invariant area density. The maximum identity gives a unique regular center; the level equation's quadratic discriminant has two positive simple endpoints and between them two positive branches. They join at the endpoints with a regular gradient, yielding exactly one compact oval for each intermediate value. Contracting the area form with a transverse field dH(X)=1 gives the smooth positive level measure on every oval, not just almost every level. The induced map is orientation preserving, so cumulative weighted length makes it translation. Substituting periods one, two and three into the recurrence rules out nonconstant marked cycles of those lengths. The sharpened near-center proof uses the independent linear parts in the sum of squares to get a positive quadratic form; radial parameterizations and the linear expansion of the map give uniform convergence to the ellipse rotation. A rational linear rotation would make the rational noninteger trace an algebraic integer; continuity then rules out a rational-only interval ending at the center. The frozen rational projection and algebra checker was read, not executed, and its finite samples are not the universal proof.
